claims.text: Jit Security’s Terraform deployment README illustrates us-east-1 AWS interface endpoints at $0.01 per AZ-hour: two AZs for 730 hours total $14.60. This illustrates the AWS-side component, not the complete current Atlas dedicated-cluster bill. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

OneUptime’s March 31, 2026 implementation guide creates the Atlas endpoint service and AWS VPC endpoint as separate resources, consistent with treating the two billing components separately. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-03-31)

Atlas bills the highest hourly capacity-unit dimension: new connections, active connections, or processed bytes. TCP unit thresholds are 800 new connections/second, 100,000 active connections, and 1 GB/hour. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Atlas adds $0.05/hour per active remote region, including partial hours. AWS likewise defines activity by at least one connected interface endpoint, rather than endpoint count. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
Atlas rates exclude AWS interface-endpoint charges; AWS bills provisioned endpoint hours separately in each Availability Zone. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Atlas AWS regional rates (USD endpoint-hour / capacity-unit-hour) include us-east-1: 0.0450 / 0.0120; us-west-1: 0.0504 / 0.0120; eu-central-1: 0.0540 / 0.0120; sa-east-1: 0.0680 / 0.0165. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

At 730 hours, one Atlas us-east-1 regional endpoint costs $32.85 before capacity units and AWS charges; this is arithmetic from the published $0.0450/hour rate, not an all-in quote. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

AWS bills provisioned interface endpoints per Availability Zone, rounds partial hours up, and generally continues hourly billing without traffic until deletion; rejection followed by service deletion also stops billing. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)
Atlas's us-east-1 example costs $0.075/hour: $0.045 fixed plus 2.5 capacity units at $0.012 each. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

AWS's active-remote-region fee is per endpoint service and remote region, regardless of how many endpoints connect from that region; partial active hours count as full hours. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)

Azure's provider pricing separates private-endpoint hours from processed data, rounds partial hours up, and lists Private Link Service itself as uncharged. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Azure's uncharged Private Link Service does not eliminate Atlas fees: Atlas lists $0.03 per processed GB across its listed Azure regions, in addition to Azure endpoint charges. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
